verify.summary:
I verified the pin change adversarially and edited no repo file. The checks as written mostly hold. build-native.sh's format check, its 8-digit comparison, the OCLJ_LUAJIT_UNPINNED values, its handling of the working directory and a relative OCLJ_REPO, both Makefiles on both hosts, and gradle's commit-field parser all resisted every malformed input I tried. That included a BOM, UTF-16, CRLF, a lone CR, a tab, upper case, 39 or 41 digits, two lines, a NUL, a directory, a fingerprint appearing twice, 7 digits, an upper-case field, and other '|LuaJIT ' strings next to the fingerprint.

Two paths still get another commit's LuaJIT code into a native stamped 1ee778a4, with no override at the build that produces it, and gradle accepts that native. Both were measured on full Windows builds:
- **Stale build copy.** The copy luajit-$PLATFORM is reused across commits. After an OCLJ_LUAJIT_UNPINNED=1 build, a pinned build in the same OCLJ_BUILD silently compiles the other commit's files.
- **Dirty checkout.** A checkout whose HEAD is at the pin but whose working tree has uncommitted changes passes the pin check.

A recorded-commit fix for the stale copy was proved in a scratch copy of the script. A read-only check for the dirty tree was prototyped on both hosts.

build.bat has a regression: it dies on a valid pin when the repo path contains ')'. Quoting the path in its four messages fixes this (measured).

Some docs overclaim, given these two gaps: the jit-guide header and CLAUDE.md say every other commit is refused. A few smaller doc and leniency nits are listed below.
findings: F1 (high) STALE BUILD COPY GETS ANOTHER COMMIT'S CODE THROUGH BOTH READERS [M]. Input: an additive build into OCLJ_BUILD=X from the clone at 8c23d6aa with OCLJ_LUAJIT_UNPINNED=1, then an ordinary pinned build (default OCLJ_LUAJIT, no override) in the same X. Observed: the second build prints 'pin = met: the checkout is at 1ee778a4', gives no warning, exits 0, and its dist DLL is stamped '1ee778a4|LuaJIT 2.1.ROLLING|412be694|...'. Yet its lj_opt_mem.o is 05d34fc1, the parent's object (equal to the unpinned step's and to impl/win-2/new-unpinned's), not 42bd49f9 (build/native's). The copy's lj_opt_mem.c differs from the pristine file by the 23 lines of the parent commit. gradle accepted that DLL (BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 'names the pinned LuaJIT commit 1ee778a4'). Evidence: verify/holes/b2-step1.log, b2-step2.log, summary.txt; verify/gruns/gc01-b2-stale-copy.log. Expected: refusal, because the copy was made from 8c23d6aa. Why it matters: build-native.sh:671-676 makes the copy only when it is absent, and OCLJ_LUAJIT_UNPINNED=1, which this change introduced, is now the sanctioned way to put another commit into an OCLJ_BUILD. In the default OCLJ_BUILD, gradle's own advice ('Rebuild it from the pinned checkout ... sh native/build-native.sh') leads straight into this. The roadmap records the gap only 'after a bump' and as [S][I]. Minimal fix: record the commit in the copy and refuse a mismatch. My scratch copy verify/fix/build-native.sh adds 7 lines. Right after `rm -rf "$LJ_WORK/.git"` it writes `printf %s "$LJ_COMMIT" > "$LJ_WORK/.oclj-luajit-commit"`. After the `fi` it fails unless `$(cat "$LJ_WORK/.oclj-luajit-commit")` equals $LJ_COMMIT, with 'Remove $LJ_WORK, or use a fresh OCLJ_BUILD'. Measured in verify/fixrun/summary.txt: a stale copy with no record is refused (f1). An UNPINNED build records 8c23d6aa and the next pinned build in that OCLJ_BUILD is refused (f2-unp, f2-pin). Two pinned builds in a row in one OCLJ_BUILD both succeed (f3-a, f3-b), and f3's 77 LuaJIT objects equal build/native's. One caveat: build/native's existing copy has no record, so the first build there after the fix is refused until that copy is removed. The alternative is to treat a missing record as 'make a fresh copy'.

F2 (high) A DIRTY CHECKOUT AT THE PIN PASSES [M]. Input: a --no-hardlinks clone at 1ee778a4 whose src/lj_opt_mem.c is the parent's, left uncommitted ('git status' shows ' M src/lj_opt_mem.c'), built with no override in a fresh OCLJ_BUILD. Observed: 'pin = met', exit 0, DLL stamped 1ee778a4, lj_opt_mem.o 05d34fc1 (the parent's object), and gradle accepted it. Evidence: verify/holes/b1.log; verify/gruns/gc02-b1-dirty-tree.log; probe p19-dirty-at-pin. Expected: refusal, or at least the UNPINNED warning, since the source is not the pinned commit. git_head reads only HEAD, and no other gate compares the tree with it (the only cleanliness check is lj_func.c's scrub line). Minimal fix: a read-only check before the copy. Run `git --git-dir=$OCLJ_LUAJIT/.git archive HEAD | tar -x -C <tmp>`, then `diff -rq --strip-trailing-cr <tmp> $OCLJ_LUAJIT`, and fail on any 'Files ... differ' line unless OCLJ_LUAJIT_UNPINNED=1, ignoring 'Only in' lines (untracked build products). I prototyped this on src/ only (verify/scripts/archcheck.sh). On Windows and in AlmaLinux 8 it flags lj-dirty (1 file) and passes the pristine checkout and lj-parent (0 files). The pristine .git/index and .git mtimes did not change. The real check should cover the whole tree, since dynasm/ also feeds the build. Do NOT use porcelain git diff or git status for this. Measured on my clones (verify/logs/dirtycheck-*.txt): in Alma a plain `git diff --quiet HEAD` calls the clean CRLF clone dirty (rc=1) unless -c core.autocrlf=true is passed. On both hosts git diff rewrote the clone's .git/index even with --no-optional-locks, which would touch the pristine checkout's .git.

F3 (medium) BUILD.BAT DIES ON A VALID PIN WHEN THE REPO PATH CONTAINS ')' [M]. Input: the layout under '...verify/bat2/paren (x)/good/' with a good pin, build.bat's lines 1-35 (CRLF) run through a wrapper. Observed: rc=255, '\good\prototype\watchdog\..\..\native\luajit\upstream.commit was unexpected at this time.' Cause: cmd expands %LJ_PIN_FILE% before it parses the parentheses, and the four `(echo [!] ... %LJ_PIN_FILE% ... & exit /b 1)` blocks are parsed even when their condition is false. HEAD's literal `set LJ_COMMIT=...` had no such exposure [S], so this is a regression for paths such as 'C:/Users/Name (Work)/'. With '&' in the path (amp&x), a good pin works but a malformed pin's message is cut at the '&' and a bogus command runs ('The system cannot find the path specified'); it still exits 1. Minimal fix: quote the path in the four messages (`pin "%LJ_PIN_FILE%" `). Measured in verify/logs/bat2-runs.txt: with that change, '(x)' with the good pin gives rc=0 and the right hash, '(x)' with a 39-digit pin gives rc=1 with the full message, and amp&x gives the full message. Plain and bang!x paths behave as before.

F4 (medium, docs) OVERCLAIMS, GIVEN F1 AND F2 [S][M]. The jit-guide header says 'build-native.sh and the jar build refuse a LuaJIT at any other commit'. CLAUDE.md line 3 says the pin is one file 'which build-native.sh and the jar build enforce'. Both checks compare commit names: the checkout's HEAD and the fingerprint field. Neither compares the code compiled, and holes/b1 and holes/b2 shipped 8c23d6aa's lj_opt_mem.c under 1ee778a4. jit-guide 7.6 ('Its own OCLJ_BUILD, always: an additive build collects into $OCLJ_BUILD/dist, and gradle refuses the unpinned native there') gives only the dist reason. The dangerous consequence is F1: later pinned builds in that OCLJ_BUILD ship the experiment's unpatched files. CLAUDE.md's 'To build at another LuaJIT commit, clone the pristine checkout into scratch and set OCLJ_LUAJIT_UNPINNED=1' omits 'with its own OCLJ_BUILD'. The roadmap's 'Still open' note limits the copy gap to 'after a bump' and marks it [S][I]; it is now [M] for an unpinned experiment too. verify.summary: I am the adversarial verifier (label: verify) of build-native.sh e1bf77df. I edited no repo file. The design's main goal, "a pinned build compiles exactly the pin's committed tree", does not hold yet. Code from another commit can still ship under the stamp 1ee778a4, and gradle accepts it. It gets in through the export itself, not through the working tree or the build copy. Two routes were measured end to end on Windows. (1) A git replace ref on the pin: the build exported the parent's tree, built lj_opt_mem.o 05d34fc1, stamped 1ee778a4, raised no WARNING, collected the DLL into dist, and gradle verifyModAssets passed (rc 0) [M]. (2) A smudge filter set through .git/info/attributes, the repo config or environment-only config (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT): git archive applies it, so the build compiled 05d34fc1 while its WARNING said the working tree's file, which here holds the pin's code, was "NOT built" and that "this native is the pin's committed tree" [M]. A third route is deliberate tampering with the object store: a forged loose blob or subtree object also exports the parent with no WARNING [M]. Forged commit and root-tree objects are refused by git itself [M]. I wrote a minimal fix in a scratch copy of the script (verify/variants/fix1, md5 5a6f8544, a 28-line diff). It disables replace objects, archives with no line-ending conversion, and checks the export against the pin's Merkle tree: every tree object must hash to its name, and every exported file must hash (git hash-object --no-filters) to the blob id the tree lists. With it, V1 still holds: Windows additive 77/77 LuaJIT and 3/3 obj files equal both the implementer's canonical build and build/native's; AlmaLinux 8 additive is 6c888050 and dropin 6c0715d1, byte-identical. negctl-bitop with OCLJ_NEGCTL_ARMS=SARCONST passes on its now all-LF Windows build copy. Every attack is either refused or builds the pin [M]. Lesser problems, all measured: on Linux, an unpinned build whose OCLJ_LUAJIT is a symlink deletes the checkout's .git; an unpinned build whose OCLJ_LUAJIT is the build copy's own path deletes its source; an unpinned build with OCLJ_OUT set to dist overwrites dist while printing 'dist left as it was'; the CHECKHOOK preflight and negctl still read the working tree as pristine. The docs' claims that the build "compiles the pin's tree as committed" need the fix before they are true. These held: refs named with the pin's 40 digits, info/attributes export-ignore, symlinked or relative OCLJ_LUAJIT in a pinned build, an unpinned build always stamping 'unpinned', every stage-1 re-take reading $LJ_SRC, the copy being remade every run, and the guide's line cites. Hygiene: build/ and the pristine checkout have nothing newer than my start, the 8 owned repo files keep their start md5s, and the only gradle call was ./gradlew --offline --no-daemon verifyModAssets on a scratch natives dir.
findings: R1 (highest; ships another commit under the pin's stamp, and gradle accepts it) [M]. Input: a scratch clone at the pin, then `git replace 1ee778a4e37122d8ca7d5733c590a47dafd6b15c 8c23d6aad7f39d58c4ca949426a3f18e900a9485 && git reset --hard`; then OCLJ_VARIANT=additive OCLJ_LUAJIT=<clone> sh native/build-native.sh (e1bf77df) into a fresh OCLJ_BUILD. Observed: `pin = met`, `working tree: no tracked file differs`, export 232=232. lj_opt_mem.o is 05d34fc1 (the parent's; the pin's is 42bd49f9), the fingerprint is `1ee778a4|LuaJIT 2.1.ROLLING|412be694|...`, the DLL is collected into dist, and gradle verifyModAssets passes ('native fingerprint names the pinned LuaJIT commit 1ee778a4', BUILD SUCCESSFUL) [M: verify/runs/w-replace.log, verify/gruns/replace.log]. The same export result in AlmaLinux 8 with git 2.43.7 [M: verify/exp/alma-probe.log]. Cause [S]: rev-parse HEAD, cat-file -e, ls-tree and archive all honour refs/replace (also reachable through GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE or a .git that is a gitfile). Expected: the pin's tree, or a refusal. Minimal fix: run every git call of the pinned path with `--no-replace-objects` (the export check in R2's fix catches what is left).

R2 (ships another commit's code, and the WARNING inverts the truth) [M]. Input: in a scratch clone at the pin, .git/info/attributes holds `src/lj_opt_mem.c filter=oclj`, and `git config filter.oclj.smudge 'cat >/dev/null; cat <parent lj_opt_mem.c>'`; then a pinned additive build. Observed: lj_opt_mem.o 05d34fc1, stamp 1ee778a4, collected into dist. The WARNING names src/lj_opt_mem.c as differing and 'NOT built', and the end line says 'this native is the pin's committed tree'. In fact the working tree's copy, which holds the pin's code, is the one not built [M: verify/runs/w-filter.log]. An unmodified clone with config from the environment only (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2: core.attributesFile=<attrs>, filter.oclj.smudge=...) exports the parent's file the same way [M: verify/exp/probe-envcfg.log]. Cause [S]: git archive runs convert_to_working_tree (filter, ident and eol) under the repo's, the global and the environment's config and attributes. The export's count check does not see content. Today this host has no attribute that changes content: the system gitattributes holds only diff drivers, and filter.lfs applies only to filter=lfs paths [M]. Minimal fix (measured as fix1, finding R4): archive with `-c core.autocrlf=false -c core.eol=lf`, then `git ls-tree -r <pin>^{tree}` and `cut -f2- | (cd export && git hash-object --no-filters --stdin-paths)` must give the same blob ids. Any conversion, filter, ident, export-ignore or forged blob then becomes a BUILD FAIL.

R3 (object-store tampering, deliberate) [M]. Input: a scratch clone at the parent, with every ref to the pin deleted and pruned. Into it go the pin's genuine commit and root tree as loose objects, a loose object under the pin's lj_opt_mem.c blob id (764cdd84) that holds the parent's file, and .git/HEAD set to the pin's 40 digits. Observed: HEAD check, cat-file -e and the count check all pass, the export is the parent's lj_opt_mem.c, and there is no WARNING [M: verify/exp/probe-forgeblob.log]. The same happens when the src subtree id (2d90cb47) holds the parent's src tree [M: probe-forgesub.log]. Git itself refuses a forged commit object and a forged root tree ('hash mismatch') on both 2.55.0.windows.5 and 2.43.7 [M: probe-forgeobj.log, alma-forge.log, probe-forgetree.log]. Fix: fix1's tree check (each tree id from `rev-parse <pin>^{tree}` and `ls-tree -r -d` must equal `cat-file tree <id> | hash-object -t tree --stdin`) plus R2's blob check.

R4 (the measured fix for R1 to R3) [M]. The scratch variant verify/variants/fix1/build-native.sh (md5 5a6f8544; diff verify/variants/fix1/fix1.diff) changes only the export block. It adds an `ljgit()` function: `git --no-replace-objects --git-dir=$LJ_CHECKOUT/.git -c core.autocrlf=false -c core.eol=lf`, the tree-object check and the blob check. Results: the Windows canonical additive build gives 77/77 + 3/3 objects EQUAL to impl/win-v1/canon-additive and to build/native [M: verify/runs/f1-canon-vs-*.md5]. AlmaLinux 8 with OCLJ_GLIBC_MAX=2.28 gives additive 6c888050 and dropin 6c0715d1 [M: runs/run-fix1-alma.txt]. The replace clone builds the pin (42bd49f9 on Windows; a96c8af7 and .so 6c888050 in Alma) with a correct WARNING. The filter, environment-config, forged-blob, forged-subtree and info/attributes export-ignore clones are each a BUILD FAIL in about 2-3 s [M: runs/run-fix1-win.txt]. negctl-bitop with SARCONST passes setup, canon, the arm and restore in 84 s on the fix1 build [M: runs/negctl-N1.log]. Side effect: the Windows export becomes LF (165 LF and 0 CRLF .c/.h/.dasc files; the build copy has 6 CRLF files after make, against 160 in the implementer's), so jit-guide 7.3's Windows line-ending facts change [M: runs/f1-eol.txt]. A build is still about 34 s.

U1 (destructive; unpinned build on Linux with a symlinked OCLJ_LUAJIT) [M mechanism, S path]. Input: in AlmaLinux 8, OCLJ_LUAJIT=<symlink to a checkout> OCLJ_LUAJIT_UNPINNED=1. :755 `cp -r "$OCLJ_LUAJIT" "$LJ_WORK"` copies the link itself, because GNU cp 8.30 -r does not dereference a command-line symlink. Then :756 `rm -rf "$LJ_WORK/.git"` deletes the real checkout's .git, and the build dies at the first re-take (:803, 'cp: same file') [S]. Measured with a probe of those two lines: 'cp -r made work a SYMLINK', 'real/.git WAS DELETED' [M: verify/exp/cpsym-alma.log, cpsym-alma-tmp.log]. On Windows Git Bash a junction is deep-copied, and .git survives [M: exp/cpjunc-win.log]. I did not run the full script on a clone, because that would delete a directory other than the build copy. HEAD's script had the same two lines, but only when the copy was missing; now it runs on every unpinned build. Expected: copy the tree's contents. Minimal fix: `mkdir "$LJ_WORK" && cp -R "$OCLJ_LUAJIT/." "$LJ_WORK/"`, plus `[ ! -L "$LJ_WORK" ] || fail` before the rm.

U2 (destructive; new with this change) [M]. Input: OCLJ_LUAJIT_UNPINNED=1 OCLJ_LUAJIT=$OCLJ_BUILD/luajit-windows-x86_64, where that directory is a clone (262 files, .git included). Observed: :709's rm -rf deletes it, and then 'BUILD FAIL: cannot copy ... to ...'. The source is gone [M: verify/runs/w-selfsrc.log]. HEAD's script kept an existing copy and deleted nothing. Minimal fix: before :709, refuse when `pwd -P` of OCLJ_LUAJIT equals, or lies under, LJ_WORK or LJ_EXPORT.

U3 (low; gradle still refuses the native) [M]. Input: an unpinned additive build with OCLJ_OUT=$OCLJ_BUILD/dist, where dist already holds a pinned DLL (1480c525). Observed: dist's DLL is replaced by the unpinned one (1b923098, `unpinned|LuaJIT 2.1.ROLLING|412be694|`), and the script prints 'NOT collected into .../dist ... (dist left as it was)' [M: verify/runs/w-unpinned-outdist.log, .before.md5, .after.md5]. That displaces the release library, which :2196-2198 says the guard prevents. Minimal fix: refuse an OCLJ_OUT that resolves to $OCLJ_BUILD/dist, at least when unpinned.

N1 (low; fails closed) [M]. The preflight CHECKHOOK gate (:443-445) still reads the checkout's working tree. A pinned build of a clone at the pin with src/lj_record.c deleted is 'BUILD FAIL: no LuaJIT source at <clone>', not the WARNING that jit-guide 7.6 promises for a tracked file missing from the checkout, although the export holds the file [M: verify/runs/w-norecord.log]. Fix: for pinned builds, check $LJ_SRC/src/lj_record.c after step 1, as the implementer did for lj_gc.h.

N2 (low; fails closed with a misleading message) [M]. negctl-bitop.sh's setup (~:661-668) runs the patch scripts on $OCLJ_LUAJIT/src (the working tree), and negctl-pack.sh's unregistered arm (:279) copies the working tree's lib_string.c. With a clone at the pin whose lj_opt_fold.c carries one uncommitted comment line, negctl-bitop exits 2: '... lj_opt_fold.c is not what native/luajit/patch-bitop-fold.sh makes of the pristine file: rebuild with build-native.sh'. Rebuilding cannot help, since a pinned build compiles the export [M: verify/runs/negctl-N2.log]. Fix: use $OCLJ_BUILD/luajit-export-$PLATFORM/src as the pristine source when it exists, and OCLJ_LUAJIT otherwise (unpinned builds remove the export).

D (docs vs code). Until R1 to R3 are fixed these claims are overclaims, refuted by measurement: the jit-guide header ('compiles the pin's tree as committed'), checklist item 2, 1.1 ('compiles the pin's tree as committed ... so the checkout's working tree is never compiled'; that half holds), 7.6 ('The working tree only feeds a WARNING ... is not built', inverted under R2), CLAUDE.md's first paragraph, README ('compiles that commit's tree as committed'), and roadmap row 203's closing note. Open question 13 says 'the canonical-object comparison of 7.6 is the check', but no build runs that comparison: R2 changed the compiled code with every gate passing [M]. With fix1, 13 can say that any conversion is a BUILD FAIL, and 7.3 needs the Windows export's LF facts (R4). The glossary's 'a pinned build reads its .git, not its working tree' is inexact: the :443 gate and the WARNING diff read the working tree (N1). 7.6's negctl sentence holds only for a clean checkout (N2). Measured claims that held: build times (about 34 s on Windows, about 14 s in Alma) [M]; the order of the preflight refusals [S]; prototype/watchdog/README.md's `git checkout "$(cat ../../../native/luajit/upstream.commit)"` path, which resolves to the repo root [S]; and 20 line cites spot-checked against e1bf77df (:322, :345-348, :369, :970-975, :1009-1014, :1080, :1138, :1153, :1230, :1611-1613, :2073, :2174, :2182, :2208 and others), all naming the stated lines [M].

Held [M unless marked]: (a) a tag and a branch both named with the pin's 40 digits and pointing at the parent: git resolves a full 40-hex string as the object, with an 'ambiguous' warning, so the pin is exported (exp/probe-reftag.log). (b) `README export-ignore` in .git/info/attributes: the count check refuses, 230 against 232 (exp/probe-1.log). (c) A symlinked OCLJ_LUAJIT and a relative one in a pinned build, in Alma: the pin is exported with no WARNING (exp/alma-probe.log). (d) A forged commit object and a forged root tree are refused by git. (e) An unpinned build stamps 'unpinned' even when HEAD is the pin. (f) Every stage-1 re-take (:800-993) reads $LJ_SRC, and the lj_gc.h gate reads the build copy [S]. (g) The copy and the export are removed on every run in both modes, and a removal that fails is a BUILD FAIL (:709-710) [S]. (h) A dropin build and then an additive one, or pinned and unpinned builds one after the other in one OCLJ_BUILD: each run remakes the copy and rm -f's the three objects of ours before compiling them (:1712, :1777, :1901) [S]. (i) The tree's own export-subst is not applied to a tree archive (the implementer's [M], gitattributes(5) [S]). (j) gradle's shape regex accepts only the pin's 8 digits [S]; R1 and R2 pass it only because they carry those 8 digits.

[I], not measured (pre-existing, not part of this change): two concurrent runs in one OCLJ_BUILD, one pinned and one unpinned, have no lock. The pinned run's link (:1952) could pick up the other run's freshly built $LJ/libluajit.a under the pinned eris_lj.o stamp. A mkdir-based lock on $OCLJ_BUILD would close it.

I implemented E1-E7 and ran W1-W7 on the final script, native/build-native.sh md5 fc4e465d. Every check passed. Of the 8 files I own, all changed. build.gradle.kts did not need to change: its refusal message already said "compiles the pin's committed tree", and that is now true.

A pinned build now makes every git call through one function, ljgit. It is `git --no-replace-objects --git-dir=<physical checkout>/.git -c core.autocrlf=false -c core.eol=lf`. The build then checks four links:
1. The pin's commit object hashes to the pin.
2. The root tree is the one named on that object's tree line, and `rev-parse <pin>^{tree}` agrees.
3. Every tree object hashes to its name.
4. Every exported file hashes to its blob id, and the export holds exactly as many files as the tree lists.

So "a pinned build compiles exactly the tree the pin's 40 digits name, up to a SHA-1 collision" is now true, and the docs say exactly what is verified.

Results:
- **W1 [M]:** Windows additive gives 77/77 + 3/3 objects equal to build/native's. The dropin equals round 2's dropin reference. In AlmaLinux 8 with OCLJ_GLIBC_MAX=2.28 the .so files are 6c88805001bae0cd2b385803f5d857c7 and 6c0715d11344c5fe075cd33f4f93cdbc, byte-identical to the release.
- **Exports [M]:** they are now the committed bytes, and byte-identical between the two hosts.
- **Attacks [M]:** every attack from both rounds either fails closed or builds the pin.
- **U1, U2, U3, N1 and N2 [M]:** all are fixed and measured.
- **gradle and hygiene [M]:** gradle accepts the pinned DLL and refuses the unpinned one. Nothing under build/ changed (38985 md5s identical, 0 files newer). The pristine checkout and its .git are unchanged (stat and md5 lists identical).

I went beyond E1-E7 in five places, listed under open questions. Evidence is in C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/pin3/impl/; the final-pass directories are named fc4e-*.

open_questions:
Do you accept my five additions beyond E1-E7?
- (a) NEGI (layoutneg-<platform>, which stage 1b removes with rm -rf) joins E3's list of directories the checkout may not be in or under; measured in u2-negi.
- (b) An unpinned copy that holds any symlink is refused. Measured reason: cp -R keeps a symlink, and the rm -f src/host/*.o that make clean runs deleted the files of the directory a symlinked src/host named (probe in fc4e-alma-w3).
- (c) The archive and ls-tree take the 40-digit tree id from the commit object's tree line, with an added check that rev-parse <pin>^{tree} agrees; the archive is still of a tree, so export-subst is still not applied.
- (d) The messages print the names (never the values) of any GIT_* variables set.
- (e) The `2>/dev/null` is removed from cat-file -e and from rev-parse ^{tree}, so git's own 'hash mismatch' errors show.

On git 2.55, link 1, and link 3 for the root tree, cannot fire, because git refuses forged commits and root trees when it parses them. Link 1 was shown to fail only through a scratch variant. Keep both as defence in depth for other gits? I have not tested packed forgeries on git 2.43.

verify.summary:
I am the adversarial verifier (label: verify) of build-native.sh fc4e465d. I edited no repo file. I measured two holes in the new directory guards (E3 and E4) and one route by which code from outside the pin's tree ships under the stamp 1ee778a4 and passes gradle.

1. **E3 can be bypassed, and the build then deletes the checkout [M].** Two spellings get an OCLJ_LUAJIT that sits at the build copy's real path past the preflight:
   - an OCLJ_BUILD written as `<dir>/<junction>/..`;
   - a different-case spelling of a non-ASCII letter.
   In both, the throwaway checkout was deleted at :879, and the run then ended "BUILD FAIL: cannot copy".
2. **E4 can be bypassed the same way [M].** With OCLJ_OUT given as `BÄU/dist` for an OCLJ_BUILD of `Bäu`, the unpinned build replaced dist's release DLL, which now carries the stamp `unpinned`, and still printed "dist left as it was".
3. **An environment CFLAGS reaches every LuaJIT compile line [M].** LuaJIT's Makefile never assigns CFLAGS, so a value set in the shell is used as is. A pinned additive build with `CFLAGS=-include <header>` reported "pin = met" and "export verified", changed 76 of the 77 LuaJIT objects (lj_opt_mem.o 228dc3d4, not 42bd49f9), was stamped `1ee778a4|LuaJIT 2.1.ROLLING|412be694`, and was collected into dist. gradle verifyModAssets then accepted it (rc 0). So "a pinned build compiles exactly the tree the pin's 40 digits name" holds for the source export, but README's "the native is that commit's code up to a SHA-1 collision" does not.

What held:
- **The export chain:** the CFLAGS run on a clean clone at the pin verified all 8 trees and 232 files [M].
- **8.3 short names:** `pwd -P` expands them, so they are not a bypass [M].
- **The new negctl pristine-source choice:** it held on reading the code (not run) [S].
- **Hygiene [M]:** nothing under build/ changed, the pristine checkout and its .git are unchanged, and all 13 repo files keep their start md5s.

I stopped after these measurements. I did not replay the git-level attacks or the AlmaLinux 8 cases, did not measure the fixes I propose in a scratch copy of the script, and did not re-check the guide's line cites. Evidence is in C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/pin3/verify/.
findings:
U2 still deletes the checkout, two ways (fc4e465d, Windows) [M]. The test checkout was a throwaway directory (MARKER.txt, .git/HEAD, src/lj_record.c) placed at the build copy's real path. Both runs used OCLJ_LUAJIT_UNPINNED=1.
- (a) OCLJ_BUILD=<E>/x/link/.., where x/link is a junction to <E>/y/sub, so the real OCLJ_BUILD is <E>/y. OCLJ_LUAJIT=<E>/y/luajit-windows-x86_64.
- (b) OCLJ_BUILD=<C>/Bäu, OCLJ_LUAJIT=<C>/BÄU/luajit-windows-x86_64.
Observed in both: no refusal. The :879 rm -rf deleted all three files, and the run ended 'BUILD FAIL: cannot copy the contents of ...' (rc 1, 2-3 s). Expected (E3): refused before any removal.
Cause [M, exp/probe-dotdot-win.log]:
- physpath (:467) and LJ_CHECKOUT (:490) use a logical `cd`, so `link/..` resolves as written: `cd x/link/.. && pwd -P` gives .../x, while ls, test and rm resolve it to .../y. The same happens on Linux [S].
- pathkey (:481) lowercases only A-Z, and `pwd -P` keeps the spelling it was given ('BÄU'), so 'bäu' and 'bÄu' compare as different.
Minimal fix, not measured in the script:
- use `cd -P --` in physpath and LJ_CHECKOUT (probe: `cd -P x/link/..` gives .../y);
- in `inside()`, walk the first path's ancestors and accept `[ "$anc" -ef "$2" ]` as well as the string match. The probe shows -ef is true for the junction, for X/LINK, and for BÄU against bäu.

U3 is still reachable through a non-ASCII case spelling (fc4e465d, Windows) [M]. Input: an unpinned additive build of a scratch clone with OCLJ_BUILD=<C>/Bäu and OCLJ_OUT=<C>/BÄU/dist; dist held a copy of build/native/dist's DLL.
- Observed: rc 0, and dist's DLL changed to one stamped 'unpinned|LuaJIT 2.1.ROLLING|412be694', while the log printed 'NOT collected into .../Bäu/dist ... (dist left as it was)'.
- Spelled <E>/q/l/../dist through a junction: dist's DLL was removed by the rm -f before the link (:2185), the link wrote elsewhere, and the run ended 'BUILD FAIL: link failed'.
- Expected (E4): refused at the preflight with dist unchanged.
- Fix: the same identity comparison as for U2 (`-ef` on the deepest existing ancestor, plus the remaining path), and `cd -P` in physpath.

Docs claims against these measurements:
- README's 'so the native is that commit's code up to a SHA-1 collision' is an overclaim [M, CFLAGS run]. The verified claim is about the source tree the build copy starts from, not the compiler's environment.
- The script comment (:442-451) and jit-guide 7.6 say the comparison uses '`cd && pwd -P`, which resolves a symlink or a Windows junction' and 'ignores case' on Windows. Both are incomplete: a `..` after a link is resolved as written, and only ASCII case is ignored [M].
- Roadmap row 203's 'refused before any removal, case-insensitively on Windows' inherits the same gap [M].
- 1.1's 'So the build copy is the pin's committed tree byte for byte' holds only before the twelve patches are applied [S].
